 For 7 Years, Veterans Day Was Not on Nov. 11. This is What Happened
 A law implemented in 1971 created a Monday holiday schedule that put Veterans Day in late October. States and veterans groups pushed back.

 Try something different:
 Show me the facts
 Explain it like I’m 5
 Give me a lighthearted recap
 Veterans Day falls on Nov. 11 every year, but that was not always so. From 1971 through 1977, the federal holiday was observed on the fourth Monday in October. The change came from a law about long weekends, and it took Congress seven years of observances to undo it.
 The 1954 Law That Created Veterans Day
 The holiday began as Armistice Day. A 1938 law made Nov. 11 a legal holiday, and an act approved June 1, 1954, amended it by “striking out the word ‘Armistice' and inserting in lieu thereof the word ‘Veterans,’” according to the Statutes at Large (68 Stat. 168). The act is titled "To honor veterans on the 11th day of November of each year, a day dedicated to world peace."
 Related: Veterans Day 2026 
 The 1968 Monday Holiday Law
 Public Law 90-363, dated June 28, 1968, rewrote the list of federal holidays in Title 5 of the U.S. Code (82 Stat. 250). It set:
 Washington's Birthday on “the third Monday in February”
 Memorial Day on “the last Monday in May” 
 Columbus Day on "the second Monday in October" 
 Veterans Day on "the fourth Monday in October"
 The law took effect in 1971.
 The VA's history of the holiday says the first Veterans Day under the new schedule was observed “with much confusion on October 25, 1971.” Its entry for 1968 says. “many states did not agree with this decision and continued to celebrate the holidays on their original dates.”
 The Pushback
 The Christian Science Monitor reported in 2014 that veterans groups “did not like this switch from the beginning.” It also said Mississippi and South Dakota kept Nov. 11 while most states followed the federal change; that Louisiana and Wisconsin returned to Nov. 11 in 1972; that seven more states followed in 1974; and that sixteen more did so in 1975.
 Related: Veterans Day 2026 
 A group of veterans arrive for an Armistice Day ceremony at the Menin Gate Memorial to the Missing in Ypres, Belgium, Tuesday, Nov. 11, 2025. (Virginia Mayo/AP) 
 Congress Reverses Course
 Public Law 94-97, approved Sept. 18, 1975, struck “Veterans Day, the fourth Monday in October” from the holiday law and inserted “Veterans Day, November 11.” The act applied “effective January 1, 1978.” The restoration was enacted in 1975 and took effect in 1978.
 The VA says President Gerald R. Ford signed the law and that it “supported the desires of the overwhelming majority of state legislatures,” along with major veterans service organizations and the American people. The Monitor quotes Ford citing “the expressed will of the overwhelming majority of our State Legislatures.”
 The other holidays in the 1968 law stayed on their Mondays, including Memorial Day.
